subject: PIC
body: Every food establishment in Dubai must have
options: at least one certified Person in Charge (PIC)
a PIC only for large hotels
explanation: The PIC supervises food safety on site.

subject: PIC
body: The Person in Charge should be
options: on site during operating hours to supervise food safety
explanation: They make sure food safety practices are followed every shift.

subject: PIC
body: A critical control point (CCP) is
options: a step where control is essential to prevent or remove a food safety hazard
explanation: Cooking is a common CCP.

subject: PIC
body: A critical limit is
options: the maximum or minimum value that must be met at a CCP
the shelf life of a product
the number of staff on duty
explanation: For example, a minimum core cooking temperature.

subject: PIC
body: When monitoring shows a critical limit has not been met, staff must
explanation: Then record what was done.

subject: PIC

explanation: Verification is the sixth principle.

explanation: Biological hazards include bacteria and viruses.

subject: PIC
body: Cleaning chemicals getting into food is a
explanation: Store chemicals away from food.

subject: PIC
body: Cross-contamination happens when
options: harmful bacteria spread from raw food to ready-to-eat food
explanation: Separate raw and ready-to-eat foods, equipment and boards.

subject: PIC
body: The temperature 'danger zone', where bacteria grow fastest, is commonly defined as
explanation: Keep cold food cold and hot food hot.

subject: PIC
body: The safest way to thaw frozen meat is
explanation: Plan ahead and keep it below 5 °C.

subject: PIC
body: Cooked food that will be stored should be
options: covered and left at room temperature
explanation: Slow cooling allows bacteria to grow.

subject: PIC
body: A probe thermometer should be
options: cleaned and sanitised before and after use
explanation: Check calibration regularly.

subject: PIC
body: Stock should be rotated using
explanation: Use older stock first.

subject: PIC
body: In a refrigerator, raw meat should be stored
options: on the bottom shelf, below ready-to-eat food
explanation: This prevents drips contaminating other food.

subject: PIC
body: A 'use by' date means
options: the food must not be used after that date
the food is best quality before that date
explanation: 'Best before' relates to quality, not safety.

subject: PIC
body: Food handlers must wash their hands
options: before handling food, after using the toilet and after handling raw food or waste
only at the start of the shift
explanation: Use soap and warm water and dry thoroughly.

subject: PIC
body: A food handler with vomiting or diarrhoea should
options: report it and stay away from food handling
explanation: They can spread foodborne illness.

subject: PIC
body: Food handlers should
options: wear clean uniforms and hair restraints and avoid jewellery
explanation: This reduces physical and biological hazards.

subject: PIC
body: Sanitising differs from cleaning because it
options: reduces microorganisms to a safe level
explanation: Clean first, then sanitise.

subject: PIC
body: Signs of a pest problem include
options: droppings, gnawed packaging and nesting material
explanation: Report pests immediately and use a licensed pest control company.
